chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one whom the [time of] Hajj catches [late], [asking if] he has caught Hajj? He said: If he arrives at Jam' while the people are at al-Mash'ar al-Haram before the sunrise, he has caught Hajj and his Umrah is not valid. And if he catches Jam' after the sunrise, it is a separate Umrah and he has no Hajj. If he wishes to stay in Mecca, he stays; and if he wishes to return to his family, he returns, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَام: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the sacred monument/station near Mina
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam', the station at al-Mash'ar al-Haram where pilgrims gather
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَة: Umrah Munfradah, a standalone pilgrimage distinct from Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who arrives late to Jam' after sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the critical distinction between Hajj and Umrah based on the timing of the Muzdalifah (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) stay relative to sunrise. It establishes that arriving before sunrise validates the Hajj component while voiding the Umrah, whereas arriving after sunrise validates the Umrah but voids the Hajj, obligating the pilgrim to return the following year. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the specific temporal conditions of the 'Arafat and Muzdalifah rites in determining the validity of the pilgrimage pillars.
